chunk-001:d73-c001-06.proposition: Neuroscientific findings about decision-making warrant limited philosophical weight because the field remains comparatively immature and common imaging methods measure neural activity only indirectly.

chunk-001:d73-c001-08.proposition: Under monism or physicalism, an antecedent brain state is part of the acting person, so neural prediction does not by itself displace personal agency.

chunk-001:d73-c001-09.proposition: Even under determinism, practically important distinctions between willing and unwilling action, including consent, remain available and support compatibilist agency.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-01.proposition: Weighted stochastic decision processes may remain randomness-like and fail to provide the unrestricted alternatives or authorship associated with libertarian freedom.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-05.proposition: Because genetics and upbringing heavily shape the criteria governing choice, criterial causation may not provide the ultimate sourcehood that libertarian responsibility requires.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: An appeal to live options needs a principled account of when alternatives are genuinely available, especially because ordinary responsibility judgments can persist in severely constrained cases.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Determinism can preserve responsibility through causal feedback, proximal agency, and character-based prediction even when inherited factors initiate development and the agent could not have acted otherwise.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Freedom and responsibility form a plural family of concepts whose practical roles in praise, blame, and interpersonal regulation should guide theory rather than a single metaphysical definition.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: A proximal-source account can distinguish choices from nonchoices under determinism without requiring ultimate self-origination, alternative possibilities, or diminished agency under decisive reasons.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: The tension between first-person inquiry and scientific self-description is a deep and near-universal epistemic problem rather than a distinctive failure of pragmatic compatibilism.
